The Bridgerton women somehow manage to look absolutely flawless even in the middle of a funeral scene.

The black lace, delicate veils and sharply structured silhouettes turn mourning into something visually unforgettable. Every detail feels carefully chosen to reflect grief without losing the elegance the series is known for. The costumes carry sadness and status at the same time. Even the darkest scenes still feel completely cinematic.

What makes the looks work is the balance between restraint and drama. Nothing feels overly flashy for the moment, yet every outfit still commands attention. The fabrics, shapes and accessories quietly communicate loss while keeping each character visually distinct. It is period styling doing emotional work without needing a single line of dialogue.

Bridgerton has always understood that fashion can tell part of the story. In scenes like this, clothing becomes part of the mood rather than just decoration. The darker palette strips away the usual romantic softness and replaces it with something more solemn and severe. Somehow, the result is still breathtaking.

There is also something very specific about how period mourningwear photographs on screen. The veils create mystery, the lace adds texture and the structured silhouettes give every entrance a sense of weight. The visual language feels heavy without becoming dull. It turns grief into one of the most striking looks the show can deliver.

Bridgerton never really switches off its visual identity, even when the story gets painful. Sorrow, beauty and drama all exist in the same frame without canceling each other out. That is why these scenes hit so hard visually. The show found a way to make mourning feel haunting, elegant and completely unforgettable.

On September 11, 2001, Seth MacFarlane was supposed to be sitting aboard American Airlines Flight 11, the plane that would later crash into the North Tower of the World Trade Center.

He missed it by minutes.

The FAMILY GUY creator had been drinking the night before and overslept. When he finally reached Boston Logan International Airport, boarding had already closed. His travel agent had also mistakenly told him the flight left later than it actually did.

So Seth went back to the terminal.

Then everything changed.

Not long afterward, Flight 11 was hijacked and crashed into the North Tower at 8:46 a.m., killing everyone aboard.
MacFarlane later said the experience did not make him feel specially chosen or protected. He described it more as a strange coincidence and a reminder of how random life can be.

One alarm clock.

A few extra minutes of sleep.

A mistaken departure time.

That was all that separated Seth MacFarlane from a flight that never reached its destination, leaving him with one of the most haunting near misses connected to September 11.

OFF CAMPUS Season 2 has officially wrapped filming, bringing the next chapter of Prime Video’s Briar University romance one major step closer to release. 

The new season shifts the spotlight to Dean Di Laurentis and Allie Hayes, with Mika Abdalla and Stephen Kalyn stepping into the central romance after Hannah and Garrett led Season 1.

Production began in Vancouver in June and had been scheduled to run through mid September, with the cast spending the summer filming the next round of relationships, hockey drama and Briar chaos. 

Season 2 will also keep Hannah and Garrett in the story while expanding the world with more of Elle Kennedy’s characters and setting up even more potential romances beyond this chapter. 

OFF CAMPUS Season 2 is now officially wrapped, and Briar U’s next love story is getting closer to Prime Video.

‘PRACTICAL MAGIC 2’ earned $4.7 million from Thursday previews and is expected to end Spider-Man’s six-week reign at No. 1.

The long-awaited sequel is currently projected to earn between $30 million and $40 million domestically during its opening. That would give the Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock-led film a strong start nearly three decades after the original arrived. The return of the Owens sisters has become one of the biggest nostalgia-driven releases of the season. Now that excitement is beginning to show up in actual ticket sales.

Internationally, Practical Magic 2 is tracking to add another $18 million to $25 million. Combined with its expected domestic performance, that would put the sequel somewhere between $48 million and $65 million worldwide during its opening. The upper end would give the film a particularly impressive launch for a supernatural sequel built around a cult classic. Its global performance is now becoming just as important as its potential No. 1 finish in North America.

The biggest storyline may be what happens at the top of the box office chart. Spider-Man has managed to hold the No. 1 position for six consecutive weeks, creating an unusually long run at the top. Practical Magic 2 is now expected to be the movie that finally interrupts that streak. If projections hold, the Owens sisters are about to pull off a pretty major box office upset.

The $4.7 million preview number gives the sequel an encouraging starting point heading into the full weekend. Bullock and Kidman returning together has been at the center of the movie’s marketing, leaning heavily into the affection that grew around the original over the years. What began as a modestly received 1998 release eventually became a cult favorite with enormous staying power. The sequel is now benefiting from decades of that accumulated nostalgia.

A global opening between $48 million and $65 million would immediately give Practical Magic 2 a strong theatrical foundation. More importantly, taking No. 1 away from Spider-Man after six weeks would turn the weekend into a much bigger headline than the raw numbers alone. Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman are bringing the Owens sisters back to theaters with serious momentum behind them. The box office spell is already working.

New first-look images have been revealed for Babies, the upcoming comedy-drama written and directed by Lauren Miller Rogen and starring Seth Rogen and Anna Kendrick. The film is set to have its world premiere at the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival on September 12.

The story follows married couple Aaron and Annie as they wrestle with the question of whether they want to have children. Their perspective changes when a close friend separates from her husband and moves into their home with her young daughter, giving the couple an unexpected look at parenthood.

Kate Berlant plays the friend, while Issa Rae also stars in the film. The cast additionally includes Dan Stevens, Ed Helms, Ashley Park, Sharon Stone and David Strathairn.

The film is deeply personal for Miller Rogen, drawing inspiration from her own experience of having a friend and her toddler-aged daughter live with her and Seth Rogen for about a year. Babies also explores friendship, caregiving and the pressure surrounding the decision to become a parent.

New stills offer a first look at Michelle Yeoh in The Surgeon, a high-stakes action thriller from John Wick producer Basil Iwanyk and director Roshan Sethi. Yeoh plays a retired surgeon who uses decades of medical expertise to turn surgical tools into lethal weapons against her captors.

New look at Seth Rogen and Anna Kendrick in BABIES, Lauren Miller Rogen’s deeply personal new comedy about one of the biggest questions couples eventually have to face.

Rogen and Kendrick play Aaron and Annie, a happily married couple who have never been completely sure whether parenthood is for them. That question suddenly becomes impossible to ignore when their newly separated friend moves into their home with her young daughter, giving them an unexpected front row seat to what raising a child actually looks like.

The story pulls heavily from Lauren Miller Rogen’s real life, including the year a friend and her toddler actually lived with her and Seth Rogen. Issa Rae, Kate Berlant and David Strathairn also star, with the film balancing the baby question alongside friendship, aging parents, grief and the pressure of deciding what your future family should look like.

BABIES premieres September 12 at the Toronto International Film Festival, and instead of asking whether a marriage can survive having children, this one asks something much messier: what if the relationship is perfectly happy and you still have no idea whether you actually want them?

The 2026 Emmy Awards will officially feature a special tribute to Dolly Parton, honoring the country music legend just weeks after her passing at the age of 80. 

Producers behind the 78th Emmys confirmed that a dedicated segment celebrating Dolly’s life and television legacy is currently being prepared, although exact details are being kept under wraps. 

Dolly had a long connection to television beyond her music, starring in variety specials, appearing across major shows and even earning an Emmy as a producer during her decades long career. 

The ceremony will also feature Noah Kahan performing “Bridge Over Troubled Water” during the annual In Memoriam segment, which will honor other television figures lost over the past year. 

The 78th Emmy Awards air September 14 on NBC and Peacock, and Dolly Parton will receive one final television tribute on one of the industry’s biggest nights.

Netflix has officially canceled Ransom Canyon after two seasons, bringing the story of Staten and Quinn to a close. Despite a creative reset and a move to an eight-episode format for Season 2, the romantic drama starring Josh Duhamel and Minka Kelly struggled to find the necessary audience to justify a third season.

Viewership data reveals a significant sophomore slump, with Season 2 opening to 43% fewer viewers than the first season. For a high-budget drama with marquee leads, the cost-versus-performance math ultimately didn't work out for the streamer.

BREAKING: Netflix has pulled the plug on RANSOM CANYON, confirming there will be no third season for the Josh Duhamel and Minka Kelly drama.

The decision comes after a noticeable drop in momentum. The first season broke into Netflix’s Global Top 10 and charted across dozens of countries, but Season 2 opened significantly lower, reportedly down around 43% from the debut season.

What makes the cancellation more frustrating is that the story was not being treated like it was finished. Creator April Blair had already spoken about ideas for Season 3, and the second season left several character arcs open instead of wrapping everything up neatly.

RANSOM CANYON lasted two seasons and 18 episodes. The ranch, the romances and the family drama are all stopping here, whether the story was ready to end or not.

Crew Girl stars Miku Martineau as Teagan Tao, a teenage rowing prodigy who steps into a prep school boys' crew as their outspoken coxswain following a family scandal. The coming-of-age series follows the team's dynamic on and off the water alongside a cast featuring Samuel Braun, Kyle Clark, and Jessica Paré.

Family scandal. An elite prep school. An all-boys rowing team. And one girl calling the shots. 📣 🚣‍♂️

Netflix is bringing the heat to the water with its new YA drama Crew Girl, premiering TODAY! We sat down with showrunner Vivian Lin to talk about diving into the hyper-competitive world of rowing and what makes 16-year-old coxswain Tegan Tao (Miku Martineau) such a force to be reckoned with.

"Teagan goes on a journey from being a solo athlete to being a teammate and a leader," Lin says, noting that the show leans into themes of found family, socio-economic divides, and serious mental toughness.

A chilling preview has arrived for Netflix's upcoming horror miniseries Below, offering viewers a first look at the oceanic nightmare awaiting a quiet coastal community. The story follows Calvin Penney, a hardened fisherman played by Josh Hartnett, whose small Newfoundland hometown is thrown into panic after the arrival of a massive iceberg coincides with deadly occurrences in the surrounding waters.

Created by Jesse McKeown, the six-episode series blends psychological tension with aquatic creature horror. As strange sonar disruptions and tragic accidents shake the island, Calvin joins forces with a visiting marine researcher, portrayed by Mackenzie Davis, to investigate the unseen monster hunting from the depths.

The footage highlights a suspenseful atmosphere filled with submerged floating houses, foggy harbors, and frightened locals scrambling to stay away from the shore. Beside Hartnett and Davis, the ensemble cast features Charlie Heaton, Rohan Campbell, Ruby Stokes, Natasha Henstridge, and Joshua Close as residents facing the mysterious threat.

Ahead of its worldwide debut on Netflix on October 8, Below is scheduled to host a special advance presentation in the Primetime section at the Toronto International Film Festival.

Margaret Qualley and Aaron Pierre are stepping into a sweeping new romance in LOVE OF YOUR LIFE, arriving in select theaters October 7 before its wider release later that month.

The film follows Maya, played by Qualley, across nearly a decade of her life as she falls in and out of love, travels the world, deals with loss and slowly figures out what she actually wants from life. Aaron Pierre plays Felix, one of the major relationships that reshapes her journey.

Rachel Morrison directs the film, with Gabriel Basso, Patrick Schwarzenegger and Catherine Keener also joining the cast as the story moves through different chapters of Maya’s life.

Different relationships, different versions of herself and nearly ten years of trying to understand what happiness really looks like. LOVE OF YOUR LIFE arrives October 7.
